definitions.explanation: Describes actions, behavior, or people that are deliberately harmful or deceptive.
Describes things of low or harmful quality, such as products, conditions, or substances.

examples.japanese: {悪質|あくしつ}な{詐欺|さぎ}に{騙|だま}された。
examples.english: I was tricked by a malicious scam.

examples.japanese: {悪質|あくしつ}な{嫌|いや}がらせが{続|つづ}いていて、{警察|けいさつ}に{相談|そうだん}した。
examples.english: The malicious harassment continued, so I consulted the police.

examples.japanese: {悪質|あくしつ}な{道路|どうろ}{状況|じょうきょう}。
この{土壌|どじょう}は{悪質|あくしつ}で{作物|さくもつ}が{育|そだ}たない。
examples.english: The soil is of poor quality and crops won't grow.

examples.japanese: {悪質|あくしつ}な{商品|しょうひん}を{売|う}りつける{業者|ぎょうしゃ}が{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: Sellers pushing poor-quality products have become a problem.

notes:
Describes something that is bad either in intention or in quality. When applied to people or actions, it implies deliberate malice; when applied to things or conditions, it means inferior or harmful quality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {悪質|あくしつ}な{詐欺|さぎ}: malicious scam/fraud
- {悪質|あくしつ}な{業者|ぎょうしゃ}: unscrupulous dealer
- {悪質|あくしつ}な{嫌|いや}がらせ: vicious harassment
- {悪質|あくしつ}な{違反|いはん}: flagrant violation
- {悪質|あくしつ}な{腫瘍|しゅよう}: malignant tumor

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悪意|あくい}: malice, ill will — refers to the intention itself, not the quality of an action
- {劣悪|れつあく}: inferior, poor — focuses on quality being extremely low
- {卑劣|ひれつ}: despicable, underhanded — emphasizes moral contempt
